name: Human Friendly Robotics Tyler
summary: Small mobile floor-tiling robot that scans the floor, plans the layout and places full tiles (ceramic, LVT, VCT or carpet tiles) while the crew does preparation, cuts, edges and finishing. Offered by the New Jersey start-up Human Friendly Robotics as a service priced per square foot installed.

germany.statusNote: Not offered in Germany or the EU. In the US the maker does not sell the robot but prices Tyler's work per installed square foot; job sites named are in the New York City area and Puerto Rico.

priceOther.market: US, robotic placement service per square foot placed (planning assumption in the maker's savings calculator; final pricing quoted per project, mobilisation and travel extra)

specs.label: Ceramic placement rate
specs.quote: About 100 sq ft an hour in ceramic placement, with ±1 mm precision and one operator alongside Tyler.

specs.label: Ceramic output per day
specs.conditions: mortar-set ceramic, one operator with Tyler; about 100 sq ft by hand (maker comparison)

specs.label: Glue-down LVT output per day
specs.conditions: one operator with Tyler; about 750 sq ft by hand (maker comparison)

specs.label: Weight
specs.quote: A 50-lb chassis drives in, plugs in, and goes to work.

specs.label: Materials
specs.conditions: porcelain, ceramic and stone set in thinset or mortar; LVT, VCT and carpet tile glue-down

specs.label: Crew
specs.conditions: crew handles preparation, materials, first row, cuts, edges and grout

notes: Rolls onto the site and plugs in; no rails or set-up crew. Onboard sensors map the floor and compute the layout without chalk lines (maker).
The placing mechanism is not described; arms set to 0 and drive assumed wheeled ('rolls onto any jobsite').
Three-year contract (Oct 2026) worth up to US$4 million with Flooring Concepts of NJ to place 15-40 % of its luxury vinyl tile work, paid per square foot.
